bug_semantics: When the optional webhook server is enabled, it listens on all interfaces and treats an empty configured token as authenticated. An unauthenticated remote POST to the configured hook path can therefore supply a JSON exec value; handleHook dispatches that value to executeShell, which passes it as the command string to the configured shell. Thus an enabled deployment with the documented empty-token setting exposes arbitrary command execution in the cc-connect process context.
flaw_origin: Single-parent feature commit 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 introduced the entire vulnerable surface in one coherent change: WebhookConfig documented token empty = no auth, an externally bound HTTP server, WebhookRequest.Exec, authenticate's empty-token allow branch, handleHook's Exec dispatch, and exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", req.Exec). This is the first writer, not a move, refactor, release/backport, revert, or merge carrier. Later commit 6feaf90f2f8cccec2203169b4d0edc3edd538837 only generalized the shell helper and preserved the attacker-controlled command sink.
ai_marker: The BIC commit object itself identifies author and committer as chenhg5 <chenhonggui@wps.cn>, and its message contains the exact standalone marker 'generated by llmgit' plus the canonical trailer 'Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>'.
evidence: Advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wfx9-6h8h-f3gm names core/webhook.go Authenticate and attacker-controlled exec, reports affected versions through 1.4.1, and lists both affected and patched versions as Unknown. First-party issue https://github.com/chenhg5/cc-connect/issues/1488 supplies the POST /hook exploit chain; maintainer chenhg5's 2026-07-03 comment explicitly confirms core/webhook.go's empty-token true branch, all-interface bind, Exec dispatch, shell execution, and config.example.toml's 'empty = no auth', then the issue is closed by the stale bot without a fix. In the validated clone, `git show 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38` adds core/webhook.go from /dev/null and adds the config and startup wiring; the new file contains WebhookRequest.Exec, `if ws.token == "" { return true }`, `go ws.executeShell(...)`, and `exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", req.Exec)`. Both `git log --all -S'if ws.token == ""' -- core/webhook.go` and `git log --all -S'Exec       string' -- core/webhook.go`, plus `git log -L :authenticate:core/webhook.go`, identify only 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 as first writer. `git diff --name-status 805045501b12fd3cf3834d19b0b882b32803e8c2 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 -- core/webhook.go` reports A, and `git cat-file -e 805045501b12fd3cf3834d19b0b882b32803e8c2:core/webhook.go` fails because that path is absent, directly proving parent absence. `git show -s --format=fuller` on the BIC exposes the llmgit line and Claude Co-Authored-By trailer quoted in ai_marker. Release checks show v1.2.2-beta.1 (ecea1ef36d86bb70dd633fb342f655d108ea52cb) lacks core/webhook.go while v1.2.2-beta.2 (9223201696e3f91b2f9fb456bba7dcef0a76bcd3) contains it, making v1.2.2-beta.2 the first affected tag. `git tag --contains 6ae088a...` includes every later release through v1.5.1-beta.1. `git rev-parse v1.4.1:core/webhook.go v1.5.0:core/webhook.go v1.5.1-beta.1:core/webhook.go HEAD:core/webhook.go` returns the same blob 6ee5088f78b1fde25178175bad9124a96e48cea6 four times; current lines 154-157 still allow empty-token authentication and lines 307-309 still execute req.Exec through shellExecCommand, whose engine.go implementation calls exec.CommandContext(ctx, shell, flag, command). Finally, `git log --all --follow -- core/webhook.go` contains only the introducer, an error-handling change, and the shell configurability refactor—no security fix. Therefore the advisory's textual upper bound 1.4.1 is stale: tagged v1.5.0, v1.5.1-beta.1, and clone HEAD 80713167d17b3f2a3906efc3b14b3acab39766e4 remain vulnerable and there is no fix SHA to record.
reasoning: The vulnerable behavior did not pre-exist the BIC: its direct parent has no webhook.go and no reachable webhook command-execution surface, while the BIC simultaneously creates the network endpoint, empty-token authentication bypass, attacker-controlled Exec field, and shell sink. History searches independently converge on this atomic feature commit; the later shell refactor merely carries the same semantics. Because the BIC commit object canonically attributes the change to Claude and explicitly says it was generated by llmgit, and this AI-attributed commit created the root-cause attack surface rather than merely exposing older flawed code, the correct verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE. The absence of a fix does not prevent a closed causal attribution because current public history proves the case remains unpatched.
